newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gonzalez should step aside - conservatives.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gonzalez should step aside - conservatives.

text.p: Spain's ruling conservatives told former Socialist prime minister Felipe Gonzalez on Saturday to face up to his responsibilities for a 1980s "dirty war" on Basque rebels and resign as opposition leader.

"He must take the political blame for the things that happened during his term as head of the government," the conservatives' deputy spokesman in congress, Fernando Lopez Amor, told the local news agency Europa Press.

The Supreme Court is considering whether to summon Gonzalez, who ruled Spain from 1982 until May this year, over the 1983-87 campaign of kidnappings, bombings, torture and murder that killed 27 people -- one-third of them by mistake.

Lopez Amor said the scandal-racked Socialists, who lost an early election they were forced to call in March, were incapable of providing a proper opposition and Gonzalez should have stepped down long ago.

"Their leaders have burned themselves out, politically and in terms of vitality, for 14 years...they are incapable not just of recovering the lost ground, but also of providing strategic guidance for a dignified opposition," Lopez Amor said.

Gonzalez has denied any role in the illegal drive against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), a separatist rebel group that has killed nearly 800 people. His first interior minister and other senior officials are on trial for the "dirty war".
